column1: # GoLean stdlib source-through — the PORTABLE-SUBSTITUTION table
# (docs/2026-09-03_stdlib-boundary-design.md §2.3.2, §6 mechanism 4;
# first slice stdlib-source-1, 2026-09-03 [AGENT]).
# A substitution swaps one UPSTREAM file of a library package for another
# UPSTREAM file of the SAME package, at the pin. No text here is ours: the
# Go project maintains both files as implementations of one contract, and
# the excluded file is the assembly-backed one (`*_native.go` body-less
# declarations + the `.s` twin, or an arch-specific `*_amd64.go`) while the
# included file is the package's own portable Go body (`*_generic.go`),
# normally selected only under a build context other than the oracle's
# GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64. The frontend's file selection is: go/build's
# selection under the oracle's context, MINUS every `drop` file of the
# package, PLUS every `add` file — and it FAILS CLOSED if a `drop` file was
# not selected or an `add` file does not exist (a re-pin that renames or
# removes a twin must surface here, never silently lower a body-less
# declaration).
# Columns: package<TAB>drop<TAB>add<TAB>reason
# Consumed by tools/nativefrontend/stdlibsource.go (go:embed); mirrored by
# docs/stdlib-admission-register.md (scripts/check-stdlib-register compares
# the two byte-for-byte via `nativefrontend --stdlib-register`).
internal/bytealg
column4: IndexByte/IndexByteString are assembly on amd64 (indexbyte_amd64.s); the generic twin is the same package's portable implementation

column1: internal/bytealg
column4: Index/IndexString are assembly on amd64 (index_amd64.s). The generic twin's Index/IndexString/Cutover bodies are `panic("unimplemented")` placeholders (NOT implementations — the frontend quarantines such bodies by name, emit.go isUnimplementedPanicBody) and it declares `const MaxBruteForce = 0`; together with MaxLen == 0 (next row) every call site is DEAD: internal/stringslite/strings.go:42 (`n <= bytealg.MaxLen` false for n >= 2) and strings/strings.go:128,167,177 (same guard) never reach them, so strings.Index/Count/Split run the pure IndexByte + Rabin-Karp paths — the exact code gc compiles for the arches without an assembly Index

column1: internal/bytealg
column4: the amd64 file's init() sets MaxLen from CPU features (internal/cpu, AVX2: 63 or 31) — a machine-specific value. Dropping it leaves `var MaxLen int` (bytealg.go) at its ZERO value — index_generic.go declares NO init() — which is what makes the previous row's placeholder bodies unreachable and selects the portable brute-force/Rabin-Karp search path; the substitution does not add an init, it removes one (the register records this init difference)
